title: Psychiatric Session SOAP Note Template (Free, 2026) | Meetily

children.text: AI-assisted SOAP-based psychiatric progress note template with session metadata, AI summary, medications, diagnoses, safety review, and audit trail.
Free template. Auto-fill from your meeting with Meetily - runs locally, available for Windows & macOS.

The psychiatric session note template is for clinicians documenting individual psychiatric or behavioral health sessions. The SOAP structure (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan) is the standard progress-note format used by most mental health practices and EHRs. This template adds an AI Session Summary section at the top so a clinician can review the auto-generated narrative before signing off, and an Audit Trail section at the bottom so the practice can keep a defensible record of AI involvement in the chart.

Use it for individual psychiatry visits, behavioral health follow-ups, and any session where you need a structured progress note. Skip it for intake assessments (which need a longer biopsychosocial template) or for group therapy notes (which need a different structure).

This is the only canonical Meetily template built for clinical workflows. Where the standard meeting template is generic, the psychiatric session template is specific to a regulated industry: it surfaces medications, diagnostic codes, safety assessment, and audit trail as first-class sections because all four are routinely required in chart audits. The AI Session Summary at the top is also specific - clinicians need a one-paragraph narrative they can quickly read and edit before signing, not a list of action items.
What the AI summary looks like

Meetily fills the AI Session Summary as one paragraph with a confidence score, then populates each SOAP section based on what the clinician and patient discussed. Medications and Diagnoses tables are conservative: they only capture entries that are explicitly mentioned in the session - the LLM does not infer medication changes from context. Safety & Risk Management is a paragraph that highlights any mention of suicidal ideation, homicidal ideation, or safety planning, flagged for clinician review. The Audit Trail is populated with the AI model version, timestamp, and a placeholder for the clinician to sign off with their name.

children.q: Who uses this psychiatric session template?
children.a: Psychiatrists, psychiatric nurse practitioners, and mental health clinicians documenting progress notes after a session. The SOAP structure is the standard format for psychiatric and behavioral health charting, and the AI Session Summary, Medications, Diagnoses, Safety, and Audit Trail sections fit the workflow of a clinician who needs a defensible, scannable note.

children.q: How does Meetily auto-fill this template safely?
children.a: Meetily records and transcribes the session locally on your Mac or Windows machine. For summarization you can choose a local LLM (Ollama) so transcript text never leaves the device, or your own API key. Recordings and audio never leave the device in any configuration. Practices documenting PHI should use local summary models to keep transcript text on the machine, or run their own compliance review before sending transcript text to a BYOK provider.

Meetily is HIPAA compliant by design when configured with local-only models - transcription is 100% on-device and no PHI leaves the machine. Meetily has not yet completed a formal third-party HIPAA attestation. A BAA is available for Enterprise customers. The Audit Trail section in this template is built to support your own compliance evidence.

children.q: Can I customize the diagnosis system column?
children.a: Yes. The template ships with both DSM and ICD support in the System column. Copy the markdown and edit it to fit your jurisdiction - the Meetily LLM follows the column schema in the template, not a hardcoded enum.

children.q: Can I download this template as Word or Google Docs?
children.a: Copy the markdown and paste it into Word, Google Docs, or any EHR that accepts markdown or plain text. Confirm with your privacy officer before pasting any session data into a cloud document editor.
